  "markdown_report": "**Proposed direction: a bounded exact-catalog ranking audit of the supplied HSTU.** At 10% research progress, establish whether sampled-pair separation conceals ranking failures before changing the backbone.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics and Industrial have training negative-win rates of 10.38% and 8.22%. This motivates auditing discrimination, but establishes no validation deficit. (2) History interventions retain only 5/1/2/5 users across categories. Such limited support cannot justify a general recency modification. (3) Category identity is null inside intervention outputs. Explicit routing is necessary before any four-category diagnostic aggregation.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Sampled evaluation can disagree with full-catalog rankings [1]. Exact ranks can expose discrepancies, while the pinned sampled benchmark remains the selection objective. (2) Rank-estimation research identifies negative-sampling bias [2]. Repeated draws measure candidate variability but do not eliminate that bias. (3) HSTU provides a compatible sequential backbone [3]. Its architecture alone does not identify which internal computation causes a ranking error.

The framework separates three questions:

| Direction | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | Exact versus sampled ranks | Training-prefix ranking only |
| History dependence | Fixed-slot paired interventions | Conditional input sensitivity |
| Mechanism localization | Controlled activation patches | Tested internal intervention only |

Three atomic proposals, scored originality/potential/difficulty on 0–10 scales; higher difficulty means harder implementation:

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact-catalog audit [1,2] | 4/8/4 | Established method; exposes candidate dependence; existing scoring hooks suffice | Limited novelty; in-sample evidence; catalog scoring costs time |
| Common-support history contrasts | 5/7/5 | Clarifies paired comparisons; supports later hypotheses; preserves architecture | Matching is established; sparse support may persist; bookkeeping is substantial |
| HSTU block-output patching [3] | 6/7/8 | More distinctive adaptation; may localize computation; requires no retraining | Intervention-dependent findings; uncertain transfer; unavailable backbone details complicate hooks |

**Selected algorithm.** Deterministically select up to 16 eligible training users per category. Use each final training event as target and its preceding, baseline-truncated history as context. Score the target once, then stream eligible catalog items in chunks. Exclude prefix-seen items except the target; exclude padding and reserved tokens. Count strictly greater and tied scores to obtain exact rank bounds and tie-aware expected hit@10.

Reuse these examples for five diagnostic draws of 99 unique uniform negatives. Report sampled-hit frequencies alongside exact ranks, training-popularity strata, coverage, and scoring cost. Average outcomes within users; report user-cluster uncertainty only with adequate support. Keep category identity explicit and leave macro diagnostics null when any category is unavailable.

Preserve the diagnostic interfaces, final-nonpadding readout, model/RNG state, all four routes, fixed seeds and training limits. Use exactly one checkpoint per category. These measurements neither infer satisfied needs nor establish validation gains.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045), [2](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/), [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152).",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Add a bounded exact-catalog training-prefix ranking audit to the family-aware HSTU diagnostic adapter, comparing exact target ranks with repeated sampled-candidate outcomes from the same single checkpoint.",
    "motivation": "The supplied diagnostics show uneven sampled training-pair separation and sparse history-intervention support. Exact catalog ranks can determine whether apparently easy loader negatives conceal stronger competing items, without assuming a recency failure or changing the official benchmark.",
    "implementation_notes": "Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Obtain category identity from the existing authorized dataset route; never infer it from item IDs. If identity is unavailable, return an explicit null reason and omit macro aggregation. Select at most 16 training users per category with a dedicated seed-42 diagnostic RNG, independently of observed scores. Keep the designated five simulator users per category unchanged. Use the final public training event as target and preceding events as context, truncated once to the baseline maximum length and left-padded. Skip empty contexts. Catalog eligibility must use the supplied ordinary-item mapping; exclude padding, reserved tokens and prefix-seen items except the target. Label repeat targets explicitly. Read log2feats(sequence) at the greatest nonpadding position. Score all items through predict_score; do not introduce a separate predictor. Score the target and catalog in the same precision and shape convention. Count greater scores g and equal-score competitors e, excluding the target itself. Rank bounds are 1+g and 1+g+e; expected hit@10 is max(0,min(e+1,10-g))/(e+1). Expected reciprocal rank is the arithmetic mean of reciprocal ranks over those e+1 positions. Exclude examples with nonfinite eligible scores and report counts and reasons rather than silently shrinking their catalogs. On identical examples, make five independent draws of 99 unique uniform negatives from that eligible catalog, excluding the target, using local diagnostic seeds. If insufficient negatives exist, retain the exact audit and mark sampled comparisons unavailable. Record per-user exact ranks, sampled-hit frequency, across-draw variability, and whether both hit and miss occurred. Derive target-popularity strata from public training counts only. Use user-level aggregation and conditional bootstrap intervals when at least two users contribute; mark very small-sample intervals descriptive. Macro-average dimensionless category outcomes only when all four categories are identified and supported; never average raw score margins across checkpoints. Save and restore every module's training flag and Python, NumPy, Torch CPU and CUDA RNG states, including exceptions. Return measured metrics, definitions, eligibility counts, null reasons, chunk sizes and scoring cost; ensure the interpreter distinguishes in-sample diagnostics from host validation. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and all category routes. Use one independently trained HSTU checkpoint per category, with no prediction averaging or score fusion. Architecture and inference remain unchanged, so retain the baseline predictor writer consistently. Diagnostics consume the shared GPU budget; only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects models.",
    "pseudocode": "save_module_flags_and_rng_states()
try:
    view.model.eval()
    with inference_mode():
        category = category_from_authorized_existing_route_or_null()
        users = deterministic_training_user_sample(seed=42, limit=16)
        for user in users:
            target, context = final_training_event_and_preceding_history(user)
            sequence = baseline_truncate_then_left_pad(context)
            if context_is_empty(sequence): record_exclusion(); continue
            last = greatest_index(sequence != 0)
            features = view.log2feats(sequence)[0, last]
            eligible = ordinary_catalog_minus_prefix_seen_except_target(sequence, target)
            target_score = view.predict_score(features, target)
            g, e = 0, 0
            for chunk in eligible_excluding_target(eligible):
                scores = view.predict_score(features, chunk)
                if any_nonfinite(scores): mark_example_invalid()
                g += count(scores > target_score)
                e += count(scores == target_score)
            if example_invalid(): record_exclusion(); continue
            record_exact_rank_bounds(1 + g, 1 + g + e)
            record_exact_tie_expected_hit_and_reciprocal_rank(g, e)
            for draw in range(5):
                negatives = sample_99_unique_eligible_items(local_rng, eligible, target)
                if unavailable(negatives): record_null_reason(); break
                record_sampled_tie_aware_outcomes(features, target, negatives)
        summarize_users_categories_popularity_strata_and_cost()
        compute_macro_only_when_all_four_categories_are_supported()
        return {'metrics': measured_results, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
finally:
    restore_module_flags_and_rng_states()

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt embeds these measured results and definitions,
# explicitly labeling all audit results as in-sample and prohibiting intent claims.",
